title: Emergent superconductivity upon disordering a topological insulator
authors: Carlos Eduardo S. P. Corsino, Hermann Freire, Anurag Banerjee
abstract: We study the emergence of superconductivity in a quantum spin Hall insulator and identify a disorder-driven enhancement of pairing arising from quantum geometry. Using sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the attractive Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hubbard model, we obtain a quantum phase transition as a function of interaction strength for different impurity densities. In the clean limit, the system develops bulk superconductivity for Hubbard interaction $\vert U \vert$ above a finite critical strength. Interestingly, strong impurities significantly reduce such $\vert U \vert$ required for the onset of superconductivity. Our calculations indicate that Cooper pairing first nucleates in subgap ring states surrounding the impurities and then evolves into a globally coherent superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that impurity-generated bound states can promote superconductivity in systems with strong quantum geometry. This mechanism is expected to be relevant in nearly flat-band systems like moiré materials where quantum geometry plays a dominant role.
summary: This work explores how introducing impurities into a topological insulator can unexpectedly enhance superconductivity. Using advanced quantum simulations, the authors show that disorder creates local bound states which act as nucleation centers for Cooper pairs. This mechanism suggests that impurity-induced physics can drive superconducting order in systems governed by strong quantum geometry.
main_problem: The study investigates how disordering a topological insulator affects the emergence of superconductivity, specifically looking for disorder-driven enhancement mechanisms.
main_result: Strong impurities significantly enhance superconductivity by lowering the critical interaction strength required for pairing. This occurs because Cooper pairing first nucleates in impurity-generated subgap ring states before achieving global coherence.
method: The research employs Auxiliary-field Quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) simulations and Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) calculations to study the superconducting order parameter.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum spin Hall insulator modeled by the attractive Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hubbard model, incorporating both interaction terms ($U$) and impurity potentials ($V$).
key_observables: Equal-time s-wave pairing correlation function ($\langle \Delta angle$), superconducting order parameter, and superconducting correlation length ($\xi_{sc}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength $|U|$, impurity density ($f$), and the orbital polarization parameter ($M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes attractive interactions are symmetric and that the mechanism of SC enhancement is driven by localized, impurity-induced bound states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the emergence of SC in clean vs. impure systems (showing lower critical $|U|$ with disorder), compare pairing correlations across different regimes, and contrast SC ordering against CDW instabilities.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the transition to superconductivity using AFQMC for bulk properties, then uses BdG calculations to resolve the spatial structure of pairing around impurities, concluding by comparing this mechanism to charge density wave instabilities.
why_interesting: The finding that disorder can *promote* superconductivity via localized states is a non-trivial many-body effect relevant to understanding unconventional superconductors in engineered quantum materials like moiré heterostructures.

In the clean limit, the system undergoes a transition from a quantum spin Hall insulator to a superconducting phase at a critical interaction strength |Uc|. (b) Superconducting correlations as a function of impurity density f for systems with topological bands at U = −6t and trivial bands U = −4t. FIG. 5. (a) Mean-field SC pairing amplitude as a function of U for different impurity concentrations. As the impurity concentration in- creases, the absolute value of the critical interaction strength |Uc|, required for the onset of superconductivity, is significantly reduced compared to the clean system. (b) Average electron density in the top layer as a function of U. (c) Average electron density in the bottom layer as a function of U. The minima in the electron density identify the critical interaction strength at which the system undergoes the transition into the superconducting phase.
